programme.title: Great Irish Interiors
programme.desc: Sitting in the majestic countryside of west Fermanagh, Florence Court was home to the Cole family for over 250 years. The original house, built around 1720 by Sir John Cole, evolved in the hands of his son and grandson to become what can be seen today. Now, it is undergoing its first major refurbishment in 25 years, presenting Collections and House Manager Rona McKnight and the team with a unique opportunity to rethink how they tell the story of the house.

programme.title: Great Irish Interiors

His journey begins at the city's magnificent fortress, the Alcazaba, Spain's second biggest Islamic fortress after the Alhambra in nearby Granada.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching For France
programme.desc: Eva takes a boat trip down the Seine with chef Eric Ripert and writer Lindsay Shapiro. Together they explore story of French gastronomy through a seven-course fine dining meal. At the heart of this delicious story is one man - Auguste Escoffier. He dominated every aspect of gastronomy; inventing and improving hundreds of classic dishes, bringing order to chaos in the kitchen with his military style brigade, and revolutionising front of house. Escoffier put French haute cuisine on the global map.

programme.title: Great Irish Interiors
programme.desc: Sitting in the majestic countryside of west Fermanagh, Florence Court was home to the Cole family for over 250 years. The original house, built around 1720 by Sir John Cole, evolved in the hands of his son and grandson to become what can be seen today. Now, it is undergoing its first major refurbishment in 25 years, presenting Collections and House Manager Rona McKnight and the team with a unique opportunity to rethink how they tell the story of the house.

programme.title: Great Irish Interiors

His journey begins at the city's magnificent fortress, the Alcazaba, Spain's second biggest Islamic fortress after the Alhambra in nearby Granada.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching For France
programme.desc: Eva takes a boat trip down the Seine with chef Eric Ripert and writer Lindsay Shapiro. Together they explore story of French gastronomy through a seven-course fine dining meal. At the heart of this delicious story is one man - Auguste Escoffier. He dominated every aspect of gastronomy; inventing and improving hundreds of classic dishes, bringing order to chaos in the kitchen with his military style brigade, and revolutionising front of house. Escoffier put French haute cuisine on the global map.

programme.desc: Sitting in the majestic countryside of west Fermanagh, Florence Court was home to the Cole family for over 250 years. The original house, built around 1720 by Sir John Cole, evolved in the hands of his son and grandson to become what can be seen today. Now, it is undergoing its first major refurbishment in 25 years, presenting Collections and House Manager Rona McKnight and the team with a unique opportunity to rethink how they tell the story of the house.

Escoffier put French haute cuisine on the global map.

Escoffier put French haute cuisine on the global map.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching For France

He dominated every aspect of gastronomy; inventing and improving hundreds of classic dishes, bringing order to chaos in the kitchen with his military style brigade, and revolutionising front of house. Escoffier put French haute cuisine on the global map.
